title: Extract telemetry emission into telemetry-fanout sidecar with adaptive backpressure
creator: Asha Kumar
description:
Problem: The runtime emits traces/metrics/logs synchronously through multiple exporter adapters (OTLP, Datadog, internal audit). Under trace-heavy workloads this increases tail latency (p95/p99) and contributes to heap pressure and transient OOMs during bursts. Multiple teams have added ad-hoc buffering which increased complexity and duplication across services.

Goal: Move telemetry emission out of hot-path process into a dedicated, lightweight sidecar service (telemetry-fanout) that provides unified buffering, per-tenant queueing, adaptive backpressure, and exporter fan-out. The runtime will hand telemetry to the sidecar over a low-overhead IPC (Unix domain socket on Linux, named pipe on Windows) using a compact framed protobuf envelope. This reduces per-request allocations in the runtime, centralizes export retry/backoff logic, and enables independent scaling/tuning.

High-level design:
- telemetry-fanout (Go): single binary; responsibilities: ingest framed telemetry, validate/enrich, route to exporters (OTLP/gRPC, Datadog/HTTP, internal audit forwarder), manage per-exporter backpressure and exponential backoff, maintain bounded memory using ring buffers and LBQ (lock-free circular queues), and surface health metrics.
- Runtime shim: lightweight emitter that serializes telemetry into compact envelope and writes to UDS non-blocking; falls back to in-process sync export if sidecar unavailable (circuit-breaker + metrics).
- Config: per-deployment memory budget, per-tenant queue depth, adaptive policy (throttle vs drop) based on SLO and customer tier.
- Observability: dashboards to monitor queue depth, export latencies, backpressure events, dropped items, and sidecar health.

Success criteria:
- 95th and 99th percentile end-to-end request latency reduction of at least 20% and 30% respectively in trace-heavy synthetic workload.
- No increase in OOM incidents attributable to telemetry emission after rollout.
- Telemetry loss (dropped items due to backpressure) below 0.05% for P0 customers under steady-state.
- Sidecar runs at least two replicas per node pool and stays within memory budgets (configurable).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime no longer performs blocking gRPC/HTTP calls for telemetry in the hot path (verified via flame graphs and instrumentation)
End-to-end latency benchmarks meeting success criteria in our perf lab (links in comments)
Telemetry-fanout has health/readiness checks and graceful shutdown preserving in-flight buffers
Configurable memory and queue limits exposed via the console and defaults documented
Integration tests for exporter fan-out, retry/backoff behavior, and fallback path (sidecar unavailable)
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy sidecar image to staging with higher logging; 2) Deploy runtime shim to small internal canary fleet with sidecar pinned; 3) Validate dashboards (queue depth, export error rate) and perf regressions for 48h; 4) Gradually increase canary to 10%, 30%, 100% with automated abort on error thresholds; 5) Rollout to Dedicated clusters with adjusted memory budgets per node type. Detailed step-by-step is in Confluence (link in comments).
risks: Initial sidecar bug could cause widespread telemetry loss — mitigated by conservative canary and circuit-breaker fallbacks
IPC compatibility across all supported OS images — need platform test matrix
Edge-case export format drift for legacy exporters — requires adapter shims and schema validation
Operational overhead of running an extra process per node (resource cost)
comments: 2026-01-18 Asha Kumar: Created ticket after incident review — bursts during a large customer eval caused runtime memory spikes correlated with exporter retries. See incident notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/2026-01-12-exporter-burst-analysis

2026-01-25 Matt Reynolds: Spike prototype implemented (uds writer + sidecar receiver). Local mem/latency benchmarks show 25% drop in p95 and ~12% CPU reduction under trace-heavy workload. Bench scripts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-bench/tree/main/telemetry-fanout

2026-02-02 Design review: decided to use framed protobuf with explicit version field to allow future schema evolution; opted for Go sidecar for fast iteration and protobuf/gRPC ecosystem. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Telemetry+Fanout+Design

2026-02-16 PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-fanout/pull/412 — basic ingest + OTLP exporter wired. Code review requested from @sylvia-chen and @diego-martin. Initial comments: prefer context-free serialization to avoid retaining runtime references; add metrics for dropped items.

2026-02-24 Matt Reynolds: Addressed code review — switched circular queue to lock-free ring with fixed-size segments and added a token-bucket throttler per exporter. Updated PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-fanout/pull/412/files

2026-02-28 Performance testing: perf-lab results attached to PR — p95 latency reduced 28%, p99 reduced 38% on the synthetic trace-heavy workload. Also measured memory headroom increase on runtime containers. Dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/telemetry/telemetry-fanout-perf
2026-03-03 QA note: Found race condition on sidecar shutdown where ring buffer head/tail could be inconsistent on very rapid restart — added graceful drain and fencing logic. Re-run tests green.

2026-03-08 Security review: quick review completed — sidecar communicates only over local IPC; exporters still require network egress rules. SRE asked to validate IAM scopes for Datadog and OTLP endpoints. See ticket: https://security.redwood.ai/requests/OBS-2026-03

2026-03-10 Rollout prep: Helm charts updated and default memory budget set to 64Mi. Created runtime shim PR to switch emitter to UDS with graceful fallback: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/815

2026-03-12 Matt Reynolds: Canary started on internal canary fleet (5% traffic). Monitoring queue depth, export errors, and runtime p99. No regressions seen in first 24h. Next step: expand to 30% if no errors over next 48h.
